records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Southwestern Greenland Inland Ice, extending westward toward the Isukasia–Ivisartoq inland margin northeast of Nuuk and the inner Nuup Kangerlua region. Nearby land, glacier and fjord names are regional anchors only; no exact terminal natural feature is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

records.supported_name_scope: Kanairiktok corridor from the upper Morris–Surf lake setting, around the long southern arc and the Shipiskan confluence, through Snegamook Lake to the Kanairiktok Bay estuary setting. Exact correspondence of the first feeder and northern lake loops remains unresolved.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Central Labrador's upper Kanairiktok corridor, separate Shipiskan confluence, Snegamook Lake and northeast Kanairiktok Bay ending distinguish this object from the Naskaupi, Churchill, Kaipokok and Ugjoktok systems.
records.region: Central and eastern Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
records.completion_scope: Representative candidate supported; complete selected-route correspondence is not claimed. The unresolved initial feeder/lake-loop section is more than a missing spelling: the readable generalized maps do not reliably distinguish its actual selected connections. This is a source-material gap, not an evidenced uncertain natural connection or completed naming-scope hold.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Initial eastern feeder and northern lake loops remain unresolved; thereafter the selected upper corridor descends through the mapped Morris–Surf setting and follows the southern arc toward the Shipiskan junction.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: No name assigned to the initial small feeder. The material hold concerns its actual lake connections, not only its hydronym.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Morris and Surf are upper-corridor lake references; Snegamook is the supported downstream lake passage. Gates and Ross identify the unresolved initial vicinity and are not confirmed selected passages. Shipiskan Lake is on a separate northern inflow and is not claimed as traversed.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Shipiskan River is a separately named confluence partner in the provincial description, not an alias for the entire selected western route. No additional tributary names are assigned.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Kanairiktok and inner Kanairiktok Bay estuary setting; no exact terminal naming vertex or current shoreline assigned.
naming_scope_details.spelling_scope: Anderson and the provincial sources use Kanairiktok River. Murphy's older report prints Canairiktok River; that is recorded only as the report's wording, not as an independently adjudicated historical alias.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative river hydronym is listed. Lake, tributary and bay names keep separate roles.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem status, piece boundaries and modeled length do not establish official naming boundaries, river length, current flow operations, historical name succession, Indigenous-name equivalence or a Korean form.

records.supported_name_scope: One selected modeled mainstem corridor. Component and infrastructure names remain separately scoped below.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Southeastern Chilamayo entry, upper-Colca northern bend, Colca canyon, southward Majes and Camaná Pacific outlet collectively identify this selection; adjacent Chili/Sumbay/Siguas/Quilca corridors and northern tributaries remain distinct.
records.completion_scope: Complete regional-scale visual correspondence of the selected corridor. Small headwater details, reservoir shorelines and exact hydronym transitions remain unresolved without leaving a substantial middle-route gap.

naming_scope_details.directly_supported_representative_name: The ARMA catalogue groups the river as Camaná-Majes-Colca; this compound is used only as the representative system identity.
naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Chilamayo is the selected southeastern component. No unselected textbook headwater or exact spring is assigned.
naming_scope_details.river_reach_scope: Colca, Majes and Camaná are successive selected trunk names, not interchangeable names for every point.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: Condoroma is an upper-Colca reservoir passage. Los Españoles is an upstream mapped structure/setting; a precise shoreline crossing or a Jayuchaca equivalence is not established.
naming_scope_details.diversion_scope: The water plan places Dique de los Españoles on Alto Colca and explains its relationship to Laguna del Indio, Jancolacaya and transfer works toward Sumbay. It separately describes Condoroma and the Tuti transfer toward Siguas. These engineered transfers are not additional selected river branches.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Named junctions locate the trunk; no tributary name is added to candidate_names.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Pacific outlet setting; no exact shoreline or tidal boundary assigned.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: Official regional cartography and water-planning material establish regional correspondence, not a formal hydronym adjudication.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled length and mainstem status are not official river length or official naming boundaries. No Korean form or historical alias equivalence established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: One representative compound only; feeder, reach, reservoir, diversion and tributary roles are kept separate.

records.supported_name_scope: Rio Mucuri is supported for the downstream trunk. The selected western feeder and northern source branch retain their separately mapped names.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual Mumbuca feeder, Mucuri do Norte junction, Mucuri do Sul incoming branch, northeast turn past Mucuri district, Carlos Chagas–Nanuque trunk and Bahia estuarine continuation distinguish this selection from a generic textbook-source route.
records.region: Northeastern Minas Gerais and southern Bahia, Brazil
records.completion_scope: Complete regional-scale review of the selected mainstem piece against readable official cartography, with municipal-map review of its actual initial feeder. Fine channel positions and exact hydronym or coastal boundaries remain outside scope.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Córrego Mumbuca → Rio Mucuri do Norte → Rio Mucuri.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: Córrego Mumbuca is the label on the actual selected initial southwestern branch in the IBGE Ladainha map. The river labelled Mucuri do Norte continues separately north of their junction; that northern continuation is not selected. No historical alias equivalence is inferred.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Mucuri do Norte is an upstream constituent reach within the one modeled mainstem piece. Mucuri do Sul and Rio Todos os Santos are contextual incoming branches and are not aliases or additional selected tributary pieces.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: No separate named lake passage or lake identity is assigned. The Santa Clara impoundment setting does not change the representative river identity.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Mucuri estuarine corridor beside Mucuri town, Bahia, in its Atlantic outlet setting; no exact shoreline, mouth cross-section or tidal limit assigned.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: Official IBGE municipal/state cartography and INEMA basin-monitoring cartography support regional correspondence. They are not treated as a formal adjudication of every hydronym boundary.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The modeled mainstem role is not an official river-name boundary. Modeled length is not official river length. No Korean name, historical naming sequence or whole-network name equivalence is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only Rio Mucuri is listed as the representative candidate; feeder, source-branch and tributary names remain in their separate roles.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
